To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the CCHCR protein is expressed in the pushing border and the lining of squamous cell carcinoma and basal cell carcinoma and correlates with the expression of the epidermal growth receptor.
CCHCR1 expression is associated with proliferation in skin cancer and that CCHCR2 is a novel tumor suppressor gene.
the expression of CCHCR 1 is up-regulated in skin cancer and associated with epidermal growth-factor receptor (EGFR) expression.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of CCHCR in the pathogenesis of SCC.
a new tumor marker for SCC, the expression of which is regulated by the tumor microenvironment.
the function of CCHCR in the context of psoriasis and skin cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CCHCR1 expression is not a marker for the development of skin cancer but may be associated with the aggressiveness of skin tumors and the expression of the EGFR.
in psoriasis and SCC, CCHCR2 is upregulated and associated with EGFR expression.
CCHCR1 expression is up-regulated in skin cancer and associated with EGFR expression.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CCHCR1 acts as a brake for the proliferation of keratinocytes in normal skin and psoriasis, but not in SCC.
CCHCR1 expression is upregulated in skin cancer, but not in psoriasis, and that CCHCR2 is a negative regulator of cell proliferation in KCs.
in psoriasis, the PSORS1 CCHCR1 allele is downregulated and in SCC, the CCHCR 1 gene is overexpressed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CCHCR1 expression may be used to identify the early stages of SCC.
CCHCR1 expression is not restricted to psoriatic KCs but is also upregulated in cutaneous SCCs and is correlated with EGFR expression.
in SCC CCHCR1 expression is associated with EGFR expression, and that CCHCR1 and EGFR may function as a positive feedback loop in SCC.
